description: 20 approved source-to-Nadi-9 translations with speaker and scene context. Note: Two examples contain deliberate legacy flaws as per specification.

examples.source: Greetings, respected mother.
examples.speaker: Elder Son
examples.notes: Shows respect prefix ka- on greeting and honorific tari for mother

examples.source: The water is flowing slowly.
examples.speaker: Farmer

examples.source: Did you see the harvest?
examples.speaker: Village Elder
examples.notes: Interrogative suffix ki at end; past tense -va

examples.source: We do not accept this price.
examples.speaker: Trader
examples.notes: Negation prefix na- attaches directly to verb mani

examples.source: Bring the green cloth inside.
examples.speaker: Weaver

examples.source: I will return before sunset.
examples.speaker: Courier

examples.source: You came back, elder brother?
examples.speaker: Younger Sister
examples.notes: da- is honorific prefix for elder brother in intimate register

examples.source: The festival begins tonight.
examples.speaker: Priest
examples.notes: Time adverb aaji rat precedes verb phrase

examples.source: Be quiet, the guard is sleeping.
examples.speaker: Youth 1

examples.source: She refused to speak the name.
examples.speaker: Neighbor
examples.notes: Refusal idiom: na-kari with infinitive stem

examples.source: Are these sheep yours?
examples.speaker: Traveler

examples.source: Our family cannot leave the land.
examples.speaker: Father

examples.source: Listen to the wind in the pines.
examples.speaker: Grandmother

examples.source: The river has swallowed the bridge.
examples.speaker: Scout

examples.source: Why are you laughing at me?
examples.speaker: Boy

examples.source: Take this coin and go in peace.
examples.target: Yo sikka lyo aur shant ja-o.
examples.speaker: Monk
examples.notes: Conjunction aur links two imperative clauses

examples.source: Deliberate legacy error 1: Do not touch the sacred urn.
examples.speaker: Clerk (Untrained)
examples.notes: FLAWED EXAMPLE: Contains raw English loanword 'touch' instead of native 'chhu-na', and violates formal register.

examples.source: Where did the blacksmith go?
examples.speaker: Customer

examples.source: Deliberate legacy error 2: The king is very angry today.
examples.speaker: Vendor
examples.notes: FLAWED EXAMPLE: Inverts meaning ('khush-ina' = happy, but source was 'very angry' [krodh-ina]). Flagged by verifier.

examples.source: May your journey be blessed.
examples.speaker: Village Elder
